qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Unrivaled scale economies shared: $713B+ top-line volume creates unbeatable purchasing leverage over suppliers, passing cost savings to consumers via Everyday Low Prices (EDLP). High-margin retail media (Walmart Connect, $6.4B run-rate) and marketplace fees increasingly subsidize core retail pricing. Proof: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 18.9% and operating ROIC of 25.7%. Primary erosion risks include Amazon digital delivery density, deep discounter expansion (Aldi), and distribution center wage inflation.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Dominant omnichannel grocery and general merchandise retailer benefiting from scale economies shared. Secular insulation across all 5 macrotrends driven by supply chain robotics automation, private label resilience, and high-margin retail media growth. Fortress balance sheet with net debt / net income ~1.1x and >12x interest coverage. [5-10Y g: traffic and volume 2.0% + pricing/inflation pass-through 1.5% + retail media and marketplace mix 1.5% - digital supply chain capex drag 0.5% + net share repurchases 1.0%]
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle compounding demonstrated by 10-year revenue growth from $486B to $713B and peak owner EPS rising from $1.46 (FY16) to $2.73 (FY25). 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 18.9% (operating ROIC 25.7%), well above the 12% hurdle. Cash generation is robust with FCF conversion of 115.5% (FY25 OCF of $41.6B easily funding $26.6B capex). Balance sheet leverage is modest with $34.6B long-term debt offset by $10.7B cash against $21.9B net income (net debt repayable in ~1.1 years; interest coverage of 12.86x). Prudent capital allocation: disciplined exits of lower-return international units (Asda, Seiyu) while scaling high-growth omnichannel assets (Flipkart, PhonePe, Walmart Connect, Symbotic automation partnership).
